name: Esarhaddon
overview: Esarhaddon was a male king of Assyria, identified in Scripture as the son of Sennacherib. His role as King of Assyria places him within the historical and biblical context of Assyrian monarchy. There are no additional notes or tribal affiliations recorded about him in the provided data.
namesAndTitles: The name Esarhaddon means 'Ashur has given a brother [for a lost son],' reflecting a specific meaning connected to the Assyrian deity Ashur. His title, King of Assyria, denotes his royal authority over the Assyrian empire, derived from the region or god Asshur. Both names are proper and titular designations found in the biblical texts 2 Kings 19:37 and 2 Chronicles 33:11.
familyAndRelationships: Esarhaddon is explicitly recorded in Scripture as the son of Sennacherib. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Esarhaddon's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his position as the successor to Sennacherib, a notable Assyrian king. His reign represents the continuation of Assyrian power during a period of interaction with the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. His mention in the Scriptures highlights the ongoing influence of Assyrian rulers in the unfolding history surrounding God's people.
